name: Diffuse Lymphatic Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse, soft, compressible, non-tender swelling involving multiple anatomical regions
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating multiloculated cystic lesions with fluid-fluid levels consistent with lymphatic malformation
Biopsy showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells without atypia
Exclusion of other vascular anomalies such as venous malformations or hemangiomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required; diagnosis primarily clinical and radiologic

searchTerms: large cystic swelling with multiple compartments
soft lump with many fluid pockets

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic imaging finding of lymphatic malformations

common.symptomName: Localized pain or discomfort due to swelling
common.notes: Often related to mass effect or secondary infection

common.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of cellulitis or infection

common.notes: Due to mass effect or fibrosis
searchTerms: loss of normal movement or use

occasional.notes: May cause sudden swelling and pain
When mediastinal or pleural lymphatic malformations are present
searchTerms: shortness of breath due to thoracic involvement

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms from spinal or intracranial extension
occasional.notes: Rare but possible in extensive disease
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from spine or brain involvement

rare.notes: Due to lymphatic leakage into pleural or peritoneal spaces
searchTerms: chyle fluid in chest or abdomen
milky fluid buildup in chest or belly

rare.symptomName: Coagulopathy secondary to localized intravascular coagulation
searchTerms: blood clotting problems due to local clot formation

rare.symptomName: Secondary bone involvement with osteolytic lesions
searchTerms: bone damage with holes or lesions

laboratory: Normal blood counts unless secondary infection or hemorrhage
Possible elevated inflammatory markers during infection
imaging: MRI showing multiloculated cystic lesions with fluid-fluid levels
Ultrasound demonstrating anechoic cystic spaces with septations
CT scan may show low-density cystic masses without enhancement
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
Rare associations with somatic mutations in PIK3CA pathway in some lymphatic malformations
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by flat endothelial cells
Lymphoscintigraphy may show impaired lymphatic drainage

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of multiloculated cystic spaces typical of lymphatic malformation
Aggressive vascular tumor with rapid growth

redFlags: Signs of airway compromise or respiratory distress
Recurrent severe infections or cellulitis in affected area
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
Gordon OK, et al. Lymphatic malformations: diagnosis and management. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019;80(2):365-377.
